checks.result: The exact implementation commit passed all 24 desktop-profile commands in 464.86 seconds, including 146 foundation tests, 22 desktop tests, 13 renderer tests within the application command, all native/application commands, 32 routes, 139 browser workflow cases, 390 keyboard cases, 64 responsive cases, and 64 visual captures. Report SHA-256: fc5e08e294efe566b636dd8131b02247bb2375968391ac07c4147ac6a3d63961.

The production bundle presents four deterministic recents and one explicit missing-location state; verifies locate/open/remove/create intent boundaries; persists canonical removal across reload; reaches an explicit empty state; recovers malformed versioned preferences without rewriting them; preserves visible state on write failure; and makes zero unexpected requests. Report SHA-256: 689cdebe6f69f861095b7b9ecf6c9f593a6de999beb4e755e006631509269f2f.

Thirteen strict renderer tests pass, including deterministic ordering, duplicate/invalid catalog denial, strict preference schema recovery, canonical idempotent removal, explicit repair, and denial of opening a missing project.
The two-file renderer implementation is exactly bound to approved reference RO-UI-ACADEMIC-MINIMAL-1.3/package db13c8d5... with no approved-reference or protected-control drift.
The authoritative backlog, campaign state, task claim, UI lineage, and generated planning views are synchronized and valid.

evidence: Recent entries use canonical UTC ordering with a stable ID tie-break, reject duplicate or malformed IDs, and apply a strict version-1 removed-ID preference record in canonical order.
Removal is persisted before the visible card disappears; reload preserves the removal, and a storage write failure leaves the card visible with an accessible error status.

The unavailable fixture exposes only Locate project and Remove. Open and Create emit opaque explicit intents and fail closed until CAP-02 project authority handles them; no path can treat the missing entry as openable or create a replacement.
Removing all entries renders the approved-style No recent projects state with an explicit link to the New Project form.
Pure tests cover success, canonical order, duplicate/malformed catalog denial, schema-version recovery, idempotent persistence, unavailable-location repair, and invalid state/action pairs.

The real production bundle exercises reload persistence, malformed-state recovery without rewrite, controlled storage failure, empty state, and exact open/locate/remove/create events across the approved Projects and New Project pages.

The README documents the versioned storage contract, opaque event API, fail-closed CAP-02 handoff, accessible status behavior, and exclusion of paths/content/credentials from preferences and diagnostics.
Renderer code owns only local UI preferences and project-selection intent composition. It imports no filesystem, service, storage implementation, credential, or project lifecycle authority.
The task-bound UI evidence preserves the approved reference identity; no reference bytes, dependencies, native privileges, or later CAP-01/CAP-02 behavior changed.

reviewerDisposition.note: Independent review must exercise the actual production bundle through available, missing, removal, reload, empty, malformed-preference, and failed-write states; confirm no implicit replacement or renderer project authority; and validate exact evidence/UI scope before approval.
